cases.question: Current AX-17 renal guidance in Germany?
cases.answer:
For normal renal function (eGFR >=90), the starting dose is 50 mg OD, maximum is 100 mg/day, and monitoring is routine [E2]. For mild renal impairment (eGFR 60-89), the starting dose is 50 mg OD, maximum is 100 mg/day, and monitoring is routine [E2]. For moderate renal impairment (eGFR 30-59), the starting dose is 25 mg OD, maximum is 50 mg/day, and monitoring is recheck 2-4 weeks [E2]; the approved German renal starting dose for moderate renal impairment is 25 mg once daily [E1]. For severe renal impairment (eGFR 15-29), the starting dose is specialist review, maximum is 25 mg/day, and monitoring is enhanced [E2].

cases.question: German AX-17 guidance before latest revision?
cases.answer:
Part 1
Historical view: documents in effect on 2026-09-14.

The superseded German guidance (DE-AX17-LBL-038), which was in effect from 2025-02-03 to 2026-09-15, stated the following historical starting doses for renal impairment: Normal, 50 mg OD [E1]; Mild, 50 mg OD [E1]; Moderate, 50 mg OD [E1]; and Severe, Not recommended [E1].

Sources
[E1] DE-AX17-LBL-038 · DE AX17 Superseded Label v3.8 · SUPERSEDED · effective 2025-02-03 · p.6, Historical renal dosing
     https://storage.cloud.google.com/tredence-fde-1-medevidence-vks/raw/DE_AX17_Superseded_Label_v3.8.pdf#page=6

Current version: DE-AX17-LBL-042 (DE AX17 Current Label v4.2), in effect since 2026-09-15. Ask for the current guidance to see it.

Part 2
The current German AX-17 guidance comprises Safety Bulletin SB-AX17-2026-09 and Current Label DE-AX17-LBL-042 [E1, E3]. Temporary hepatic monitoring enhancement requires baseline hepatic laboratory values with repeat testing between Day 14 and Day 21 [E1]. Action thresholds include ALT/AST >3x ULN requiring medical review, bilirubin >2x ULN requiring urgent review, and a mild isolated change below trigger requiring a repeat test [E2]. The approved German renal starting dose for moderate renal impairment is 25 mg once daily [E1, E3]. Renal dose modifications are: Normal with eGFR >=90 has a starting dose of 50 mg OD, maximum of 100 mg/day, and routine monitoring [E4]; Mild with eGFR 60-89 has a starting dose of 50 mg OD, maximum of 100 mg/day, and routine monitoring [E4]; Moderate with eGFR 30-59 has a starting dose of 25 mg OD, maximum of 50 mg/day, and monitoring to recheck 2-4 weeks [E4]; Severe with eGFR 15-29 has a specialist review starting dose, maximum of 25 mg/day, and enhanced monitoring [E4].

cases.question: Compare AE evidence in HN-204 and HN-311.
cases.answer:
In HN-204, treatment-emergent adverse event rates for AX-17 % and Control % are: nausea 12.7% and 6.0% [E1], headache 14.0% and 6.6% [E1], fatigue 15.3% and 7.2% [E1], dizziness 16.6% and 7.8% [E1], rash 17.8% and 8.4% [E1], and transaminase elevation 19.1% and 9.0% [E1]. The highest treatment % in HN-204 is 19.1 [E4]. In HN-311, treatment-emergent adverse event rates for AX-17 % and Control % are: nausea 11.8% and 6.0% [E2], headache 13.0% and 6.6% [E2], fatigue 14.2% and 7.2% [E2], dizziness 15.4% and 7.8% [E2], rash 16.6% and 8.4% [E2], and transaminase elevation 17.7% and 9.0% [E2]. The highest treatment % in HN-311 is 17.7 [E4]. Control % differences (HN-311 minus HN-204) are +0.0 points [E4]. Treatment % differences (HN-311 minus HN-204) are -0.9 points for nausea, -1.0 points for headache, -1.1 points for fatigue, -1.2 points for dizziness, -1.2 points for rash, and -1.4 points for transaminase elevation [E4]. All treatment % differences (HN-311 minus HN-204) lie between -1.4 and -0.9 points [E4].

Sources
[E1] HN-204 · HN-204 Clinical Study v1.0 · APPROVED · effective 2025-06-12 · p.11, Table 14
     https://storage.cloud.google.com/tredence-fde-1-medevidence-vks/raw/HN-204_Clinical_Study.pdf#page=11
[E2] HN-311 · HN-311 Clinical Study v1.0 · APPROVED · effective 2026-01-18 · p.11, Table 14
     https://storage.cloud.google.com/tredence-fde-1-medevidence-vks/raw/HN-311_Clinical_Study.pdf#page=11
[E4] computed by code from [E3] (differences and highest values; not document text)

cases.question: Which study had the highest rash rate, and what is the current renal starting dose for moderate impairment in Germany?
cases.answer:
Part 1
Result of a read-only query on v_adverse_events (1 row):

| study_id | treatment_rate_pct |
|-|-|
| HN-402 | 19.7 |

SQL:
SELECT study_id, treatment_rate_pct
FROM `tredence-fde-1.medevidence_v1_vks.v_adverse_events`
WHERE LOWER(event) = 'rash'
ORDER BY treatment_rate_pct DESC
LIMIT 1

Part 2
The current renal starting dose for moderate impairment in Germany is 25 mg OD [E2].

Sources
[E2] DE-AX17-LBL-042 · DE AX17 Current Label v4.2 · APPROVED · effective 2026-09-15 · p.6, Table 3
